## Why `slurmpilot`?

Running large Monte Carlo power studies, hierarchical models, or bootstraps on a
SLURM cluster usually forces researchers into manual batch scripting and blind
guesses for `--mem`, `--time`, and array chunking. `slurmpilot` replaces that
guesswork with an empirical, reproducible four-stage pipeline:

1. **Micro-pilot profiling (`pilot_run()`):** Executes a small sample slice in
   isolated child R processes while polling real OS resident memory (RSS) via
   `ps`.
2. **Resource auto-sizing (`estimate_resources()`):** Computes optimal array
   chunk sizes, `--mem`, `--time`, and `--cpus-per-task` flags with tail-safe
   margins.
3. **Pluggable execution (`MockSlurmBackend` / `SlurmSshBackend`):** Develop
   and test the complete lifecycle locally in parallel background R processes on
   a laptop, then switch to SSH/SLURM with zero workflow rewrites.
4. **Atomic checkpoints & surgical retries (`slurm_retry()`, `slurm_collect()`):**
   Every chunk writes an atomic `.rds` checkpoint protected by a SHA-256 sidecar
   so failed or OOM chunks retry cleanly without recomputing completed work.

## Quickstart: Five-Minute Local-to-Cluster Pipeline

Define a lightweight simulation task list and worker function:

```{r define-workload}
library(slurmpilot)

tasks <- lapply(seq_len(12L), function(i) {
  list(task_id = i, n = 60L, effect = 0.35, reps = 50L)
})

power_worker <- function(cfg) {
  rejects <- replicate(cfg$reps, {
    x <- stats::rnorm(cfg$n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
    y <- stats::rnorm(cfg$n, mean = cfg$effect, sd = 1)
    stats::t.test(y, x)$p.value < 0.05
  })
  data.frame(
    task_id = cfg$task_id,
    empirical_power = mean(rejects)
  )
}
```

Before staging a workload, run `inspect_job_globals()` to verify that your
worker does not accidentally capture large local objects or miss helper
functions:

```{r inspect-globals}
audit <- inspect_job_globals(power_worker, args_list = tasks)
print(audit)
```

Now run a quick empirical micro-pilot (`n_pilot = 2L`), auto-size SLURM
resources, and execute on `MockSlurmBackend` (strictly capped at 2 local
workers):

```{r pilot-and-run}
pilot <- pilot_run(
  fun = power_worker,
  args_list = tasks,
  n_pilot = 2L,
  seed = 2026L
)
print(pilot)

resources <- estimate_resources(
  pilot = pilot,
  n_tasks = length(tasks),
  max_chunk_size = 4L
)
print(resources)

tmp_root <- tempfile("sp_gs_")
backend <- mock_slurm_backend(root_dir = tmp_root, max_workers = 2L)

job <- slurm_submit(
  backend = backend,
  fun = power_worker,
  args_list = tasks,
  resources = resources,
  name = "quickstart_power",
  seed = 2026L
)

status <- slurm_wait(job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05)
print(status)

results <- slurm_collect(job, simplify = TRUE)
head(results)
```

## One-Call Autopilot

For everyday runs, `slurm_autopilot()` orchestrates piloting, sizing,
submission, waiting, automatic adaptive retries, and result collection in one
function call:

```{r autopilot}
tmp_auto <- tempfile("sp_auto_")
auto_backend <- mock_slurm_backend(root_dir = tmp_auto, max_workers = 2L)

run <- slurm_autopilot(
  fun = function(x) data.frame(id = x, squared = x^2),
  args_list = as.list(seq_len(8L)),
  backend = auto_backend,
  n_pilot = 2L,
  max_chunk_size = 4L,
  auto_retry = 1L,
  simplify = TRUE,
  poll_interval = 0.05
)

print(run)
run$results

unlink(c(tmp_root, tmp_auto), recursive = TRUE)
```
